label: indef
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{indef}
All nonsingular skew-symmetric matrices over $\mathbb{F}$ are congruent, and all nonsingular complex symmetric matrices are congruent; see
\cite[Corollaries 4.4.4, 4.4.19]{HornJohn},\cite[Theorem 2.5]{Thomp}.
Thus, by Proposition~\ref{conj}, centralizers of elements of an $H$-orthogonal/$H$-symplectic group can be transferred via congruence to the corresponding standard forms of $H$.
                                                                                                                                                           
Similarly, by Sylvester's inertia theorem, centralizers of elements of $\mathop{\rm U}\nolimits(n,H)$ are isomorphic to those of the corresponding elements of $\mathop{\rm U}\nolimits(p,q)$, where $H$ is congruent to $I_{p,q}$.

label: exW
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exW} (cf. \cite[Example 3.1]{TSOS}) Let $^{\star}$ denote either transpose $^{T}$ or conjugate transpose $^{*}$.
Fix $d\in \{0,1\}$, $\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}$, and suppose $\alpha_{1}>\ldots >\alpha_{N}$,
$m_1,\ldots,m_N\in \mathbb{N}$. For $r\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ let $B_{r}$ be nonsingular with
                                                                          
$B_{r}^{\star}=\varepsilon^{\alpha_r+d-1}B_{r}$, and let 
$Z_{j}^{r}$ 
                                                                              
satisfy $(Z_j^{r})^{\star}=-\varepsilon^{\alpha_r-j+d-1}Z_{j}^{r}$; all matrices are of size $m_r\times m_r$.
Define a matrix of the form (\ref{0T0}):
 
\small
\begin{align}\label{asZ}
&\mathcal{W}=\bigoplus_{r=1}^{N}T(I_{m_r},W_1^{r},\ldots,W_{\alpha_r-1}^{r})\in \mathbb{T}^{\alpha,\mu},\qquad
W_{j}^{r}:=B_{r}^{-1}\big(Z_{j}^{r}-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\varepsilon^k(W_k^{r})^{\star}B_{r}W_{j-k}^{r}
\big).
\end{align}

title: Example
body_md:
Suppose we are given an $H$-orthogonal matrix $\mathcal{R}$:
\[
\mathcal{R}=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m}\Big(\exp \big( J_2(0)\big) \oplus \exp \big(-(J_2(0))^{T} \big) \Big)\oplus I_k, \qquad
H=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m}\begin{bsmallmatrix}
0 & I_{2}\\
 I_{2} & 0
\end{bsmallmatrix}\oplus I_k,
\]
                                         
Using Algorithm \ref{algo} from Lemma \ref{EqT} and generators from Examples \ref{exW}, \ref{exF} for $d=0$, $\star=T$, $\varepsilon=-1$, the centralizer $\mathop{\rm C}\nolimits_{\mathop{\rm O}\nolimits_n(\mathbb{C},H)}(\mathcal{R})$, with $n:=4m+k$, is conjugate to a group consisting of matrices of the form:
\small
\[
\begin{bmatrix}[cc|c]
A_0 & A_0 J_m^{-1}Z & -A_0 J_m^{-1} F^T\widetilde{A}_0  \\           
0   & A_0 & 0 \\        
\hline
0   & F   & \widetilde{A}_0          
\end{bmatrix}
=
\big((A_0\oplus A_0)\oplus \widetilde{A}_0\big)
\begin{bsmallmatrix}
       
I_{2m} & J_m^{-1}Z & 0  \\           
0   & I_{2m} & 0 \\        
\hline
0   & 0   & I_{k}          
\end{bsmallmatrix}
\begin{bsmallmatrix}
       
I_{2m} & 0 & -J_m^{-1} F^T\widetilde{A}_0  \\           
0   & I_{2m} & 0 \\        
\hline
0   & \widetilde{A}_0^{T}F   & I_{2m}          
\end{bsmallmatrix},
\]
\normalsize
where
                  
$\widetilde{A}_0\in \mathop{\rm O}\nolimits_k(\mathbb{C})$, 
       
$A_0\in \mathop{\rm Sp}\nolimits_{2m}(\mathbb{C},J_m)$,
      
$J_m=\begin{bsmallmatrix}
0 & I_{m}\\
- I_{m} & 0
\end{bsmallmatrix}$,
$F\in \mathbb{C}^{k\times 2m}$,
        
$Z=-Z^T\in \mathbb{C}^{2m\times 2m}$.

label: stabw2Ri
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{stabw2Ri}
For $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N)$ with $\alpha_{1}>\ldots >\alpha_{N}$, 
$\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_N)$, set $n:=2\sum_{r=1}^N \alpha_r m_r$, and let $\mathbb{T}^{\alpha,\mu}$ be as in (\ref{0T0}) with $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}$.
Fix $d\in \{0,1\}$, $a,b>0$ and define
 
\begin{align*}
& 
\mathcal{A}^{}:=\bigoplus_{r=1}^{N}\Big(\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m_r}\big(J_{\alpha_r}^{\mathbb{R}}(a,b)\oplus -(J_{\alpha_r}^{\mathbb{R}}(a,b))^T\big)\Big), \qquad
\mathcal{R}:=e^{\mathcal{A}}, \\
                                 
&
\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits= 
\left\{
\begin{array}{ll}
\hspace{-1.5mm}               
\mathop{\rm O}\nolimits_{n}(\mathbb{R},H),   &  \hspace{-1.5mm} 
d = 0\\
\hspace{-1.5mm}             
\mathop{\rm Sp}\nolimits_{n}(\mathbb{R},H),      &   \hspace{-1.5mm} 
d = 1
\end{array}
\right.\hspace{-2mm}, \qquad 
H=\bigoplus_{r=1}^{N} \Big( \bigoplus_{j=1}^{m_r} 
\begin{bsmallmatrix}
0 & I_{\alpha_r}\\
 (-1)^{d} I_{\alpha_r} & 0
\end{bsmallmatrix}\Big).
\end{align*}
 
Then 
                    
$\Sigma_{\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits}\big(\mathcal{A}^{})\big)$ and 
                 
$\mathop{\rm C}\nolimits_{\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits}(\mathcal{R}^{})$
coincide, and they are conjugate (over $\mathbb{C}$) to the group 
\[
\mathbb{X}:=\{\mathcal{X}\oplus (\mathcal{X}^{-1})^{T}\oplus \overline{\mathcal{X}}\oplus (\overline{\mathcal{X}}^{-1})^{T} \mid \mathcal{X}\in \mathbb{T}^{\alpha,\mu}\}, \quad
\mathop{\rm dim}\nolimits_{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{X})=2\sum_{r=1}^{N} m_r\big(\alpha_r m_r+2\sum_{s=1}^{r-1}\alpha_s m_s\big).
\]

label: OpI
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{OpI}
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\roman*)},ref={\roman*},wide=0pt,itemsep=5pt]
 
\item \label{OpIi} In comparison with \cite[Theorem 2.3]{TSOC} and \cite[Theorem 3.2]{TSOS}, 
Theorems \ref{stabw1}-\ref{stabw2Ri} and Theorem \ref{stabwU} for real eigenvalues exhibit a particularly simple situation:
the group $\mathbb X$ has the particularly simple form $\mathbb {X}\cong\mathbb {T}^{\alpha,\mu}$. In the remaining cases, the parametrization of $\mathbb X$ is given recursively by Lemma~\ref{EqT}, through Algorithm~\ref{algo}.
Moreover, all proofs provide a matrix $\Psi$ satisfying $\mathop{\rm C}\nolimits_{\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits}({\mathcal{R}^{}_{}})=\Psi^{-1} \mathbb{X} \Psi $; see (\ref{psi0}), (\ref{QPsi}), (\ref{QPsiU}).
 
\item \label{OpIii} Theorems \ref{stabw1}-\ref{stabw2Ri} do not follow directly from Theorem \ref{stabw2}, which treats the nilpotent/unipotent case.
Indeed, the centralizers $\mathop{\rm C}\nolimits_{\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits}(S)$, $\mathop{\rm C}\nolimits_{\mathop{\rm G}\nolimits}(U)$ of the components in the Jordan-Chevalley decomposition $R=SU$ admit nice descriptions up to con\-ju\-ga\-tion by different matrices. Determining their intersection is therefore nontrivial.
\end{enumerate}

title: Example
body_md:
We solve $\mathcal{F}\mathcal{X}^{T}\mathcal{F}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{X}=\mathcal{B}$ for $\mathcal{F}=E_3(I)\oplus E_2(I)$, $\mathcal{B}=(J\oplus -J\oplus J)\oplus (I \oplus -I)$, with the identity $I$, 
                                 
$J^T=-J$, and $\mathcal{X}$ partitioned conformally to $\mathcal{B}$: 
         
 
\small
                              
\begin{align*}
        
\mathcal{B}=(\mathcal{F}\mathcal{X}^{T}\mathcal{F})(\mathcal{B}\mathcal{X})
=\begin{bmatrix}[ccc|c c]
A_1^{T} & B_1^{T} & C_1^{T}  &  P^{T}  &  Q^{T} \\                
0   & A_1^{T} & B_1^{T}     &  0      &   P^{T} \\          
0   & 0   & A_1^{T}      &  0   & 0   \\           
                                         
\hline
0    & M^{T}  & N^{T}    &  A_2^{T}  &  B_2^{T} \\                
 0   & 0     & M^{T}     &  0       &   A_2 ^{T}           
       
                                                                            
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}[ccc|cc]
JA_1 & JB_1 & JC_1  &  JM  &  JN \\            
0   & -JA_1 & -JB_1    &  0  &   -J M  \\          
0   & 0   & J A_1     &  0  & 0   \\           
                                                 
\hline
0     & P  & Q                &  A_2    &  B_2 \\            
0     & 0   & -P              &  0    &  -A_2             
       
                                                                    
\end{bmatrix}=
   
\end{align*}
            
       
                              
\begin{align*}
  
=
\begin{bmatrix}[ccc|cc]
A_1^{T}JA_1 & A_1^{T}JB_1\hspace{-0.5mm}-\hspace{-0.5mm}B_1^{T} J A_1 & A_1^{T}J C_1\hspace{-0.5mm}+\hspace{-0.5mm}C_1^{T}J A_1\hspace{-0.5mm}-\hspace{-0.5mm}B_1^{T}J  B_1    & \hspace{-0.5mm} A_1^{T}JM\hspace{-0.5mm}+\hspace{-0.5mm}P^{T}A_2 \hspace{-0.5mm} &  A_1^{T}J N+B_1^{T}JM  \\ 
& & + P^{T}Q - Q^{T} P & & + P^{T}B_2- Q^{T}A_2 \\                             
                                                                                                                                                              
  0         & -A_1^{T}JA_1 &  -A_1^{T} J B_1 +B_1^{T}J A_1    &  0   &   -A_1^{T}JM - P^{T}A_2 \\         
                                                                                                                                            
0   &     0                  & A_1^{T}J A_1                        &  0  & 0             \\                       
                                                       
\hline 
   &    &                     &  A_{2}^{T} A_2       &   A_2^{T}B_2 - B_2^{T} A_2 \\ 
	 &    &                     &                       &     -M^{T}JM                          \\
	                            
   &    &                       &      0           &    + A_2^{T}A_2                                       
                                                                          
       
                                                          
\end{bmatrix}
\end{align*}
\normalsize
 
\begin{itemize}[
                                     
wide=12pt,itemsep=2pt,leftmargin=25pt]
\item Choose $P,Q$ arbitra\-rily.
 
\item By comparing the main diagonal blocks we get $A_1$ and $A_2$ ($J=A_1^{T} J A_1$, $I=A_2^{T}A_2$).
                                             

\item The $(1,1)$-block of the upper right block gives $A_1^{T}JM+P^{T}A_2=0$, 
so $M=-A_1^{} J^{-1}P^{T}A_2$. 
 
\item The first superdiagonals yield $A_1^{T}JB_1-B_1^{T} J A_1=0$, $A_2^{T}B_2 - B_2^{T} A_2-M^{T}JM=0$ and $A_1^{T}JN-B_1^{T}M+P^{T}B_2-Q^{T}A_2$, thus $B_1=A_1J^{-1}Z_1$ for some $Z_1=-Z_1^{T}$,
                  
$B_2=\frac{1}{2}A_2 M^{T}JM+ A_2 Z_2$ for some $Z_2=Z_2^{T}$,
             
$N=A_1 J^{-1}(B_1^{T}M-P^{T}B_2+Q^{T}A_2)$.
                
 
\item Finally, the second superdiagonal yields $A_1^{T}J C_1+C_1^{T}J A_1-B_1^{T}J B_1 + P^{T}Q - Q^{T} P=0$, 
therefore $C_1=A_1 J^{-1} Z_3+\frac{1}{2}A_1 J^{-1}(B_1^{T}J B_1 - P^{T}Q + Q^{T} P)
                                     
$ with $Z_3^T=Z_3$.
\end{itemize}
